question: Distinguish between marginal costing and absorption costing.
sources: Marginal costing and absorption costing principles

points.label: Treatment of fixed costs
points.description: Under marginal costing fixed costs are period costs charged to profit; under absorption costing they are part of product cost.
points.basis: Marginal costing: treatment of fixed costs

points.label: Valuation of inventory
points.description: Marginal costing values closing stock at variable cost only; absorption costing includes a share of fixed production overheads.
points.basis: Marginal costing vs absorption costing: inventory valuation

points.label: Difference in profit
points.description: When opening and closing stock levels differ, the two methods give different profits because fixed overhead is carried in stock under absorption costing.
points.basis: Marginal costing vs absorption costing: reconciliation of profit

points.label: Presentation
points.description: Marginal costing shows contribution (sales less variable cost); absorption costing shows gross profit after full production cost.

points.label: Use in decisions
points.description: Marginal costing is more useful for short-term decisions such as make or buy, pricing and product mix; absorption costing suits external reporting and long-term pricing.
points.basis: Marginal costing: use in managerial decisions
